Publishing pitch October 2026

Sixteen hovering robots, five rounds, one vault each

A 16-player online party game where hovering robots dash, jump and slam each other off the map for money. Built solo on deterministic rollback netcode, finished rather than Early Access, and looking for a publisher to help it get seen.

01

The game

RoboSquare: Recharged is an online multiplayer party game about hovering robots and the appalling things they do to each other. Up to 16 players drop into a lobby, play five randomly chosen minigames back to back, and bank what they earn every round until the bot with the biggest vault is crowned champion.

Your bot floats, which sounds elegant until you realize floating things do not stop when you want them to. Momentum is your best weapon and your worst habit.

Mid round, things go wrong on purpose. Gravity gets lazy, bombs start falling, and a UFO turns up to help itself to whoever is winning.

There is no meta to study and no loadout to optimize. There is you, a floating metal square, and fifteen other people who would very much like you to be somewhere else. Ideally off the edge.

It ships as a finished game, and everything in this deck is in the build today.

02

Five rounds, one vault, biggest vault wins

1The lobby fillsUp to 16 players. Steam friends party up and arrive together.
2Five rounds get drawnMode and arena are picked at random each round, from five modes and 17 arenas.
3Every round paysWhatever a bot earns goes into its vault and stays at risk all match. Other bots can take a cut.

The money in a match is just the score. It resets every game, it cannot be bought and it does not buy anything. One running total means the player in last place after round two still has a route back, and the leader always has something to lose.

03

Every mode is a different way to get paid

Five randomly chosen minigames per match. Two of them are not about shoving anyone off anything, which is the main thing that separates this from the first RoboSquare.

Every arena is built

17 of 17

All seventeen are in the build and in rotation. Four of them are a week old: I built Citadel Run, Ziggurat Ascent, Gemini Crossing and Midline in seven days.

Plus a menu, a lobby and a tutorial

04

Three buttons, eight ways it goes wrong

JUMPGet airborne, clear a gap, or leave the ground before someone else decides you should.
DASHClose distance fast, steal a drop-off, or ram a stranger into a pit.
SLAMDrop out of the sky like a wrecking ball and launch everyone nearby into the sunset.

That is the whole control scheme. It takes about forty seconds to learn and considerably longer to stop being bad at, because every one of those three spends energy and every hit you take rattles you a little more.

Then, mid round and unannounced, the arena stops cooperating. These are the eight events currently in rotation:

Wind Storm Low Gravity Falling Bombs High Instability UFOs Cyber Pirates Clone Surge Energy Overload

Clone Surge gives everyone a duplicate wearing their own name and paint, which pops the moment anybody touches it. You cannot plan for any of it. That is the point, and it is also what makes clips.

05

Why it seats sixteen

Most party games seat four, or eight, or twelve. A group of six splits and two people watch. Sixteen seats means the whole Discord gets in at once. That was the design goal from the first day.

Sixteen robots colliding at once is a netcode problem before it is a design one. Recharged runs on Photon Quantum 3, a deterministic rollback simulation, which is the same class of technology fighting games use. Every client runs the same simulation and agrees on the result. It took longer than anything else in the project and it is the part I am proudest of.

Already in the build

  • Full controller support (Xbox, DualShock, DualSense)
  • Steam friends party up and join together
  • Rejoin a match you dropped out of
  • Steam achievements, global leaderboards, cloud saves, Family Sharing
  • 14 bodies, 6 hover thrusters, 6 finishes, plus body and thruster colors
  • Per-player stat tracking, end of match accolades, and an automatic rival
06

I have shipped this game once already

I released RoboSquare on 31 December 2021. Free-to-play, and three modes that all came down to the same thing: push the other robot off the platform.

53,926lifetime unique players on Steam
77%positive across nearly 250 reviews
29.92MSteam store page impressions

One complaint came up over and over in those reviews: there is not enough of it. They were right, and I could not fix it without rebuilding the whole thing. That is what Recharged is.

What actually changed
 RoboSquare, 2021Recharged
Modes3, all variations on one shove5, two of them not shove based
ArenasNever published17
NetcodeNot rollbackPhoton Quantum 3 deterministic rollback
ControllerPartialFull
ModelEarly Access, then free-to-playPremium, finished at launch
Both games seat sixteen players, so that is deliberately not a row. Anyone who played the first one would know.
07

The competitive party slot is open

Almost every friend-group hit of the last two years is co-op. What almost nobody is shipping is competitive party PvP, the Fall Guys slot, and it has been sitting open while everything next to it sold.

The obvious objection is that this is a Fall Guys clone. My answer is three things Fall Guys does not have: 16-player deterministic rollback netcode, five distinct competitive modes rather than one obstacle-course format, and eight chaos events that wreck the round on purpose. I chose the comparison, and it is doing work for me.

Fall GuysThe anchor everyone understands in one sentence.
Super Battle Golf100,000 copies in its first 48 hours in 2026. Proof that PvP party sells now, through friend-group channels.
PEAK, R.E.P.O.Cheap, low-friction, high-chaos games bought because friends already own them. A durable category, and mostly co-op.
Gang Beasts, Party AnimalsPhysics comedy multiplayer keeps selling for years.

I have a day job. This is the thing I do instead of evenings.

09

How it makes money

Premium purchase up front at $5.99 USD, releasing on Steam in Q1 2027 as a full release. On top of that, cosmetics only, and nothing that changes a match.

Crates and keys both drop from playing, daily, for everyone. If you do not want to wait, you can buy keys. That is the whole monetization.

I built the economy myself on Steam Inventory, and everything in it can be earned by playing.

10

The ask

What I want

  • Reach. Creator and press relationships. This genre sells when a friend group plays it on camera, and I am one person with an inbox
  • A launch. Someone who has landed a multiplayer release before: timing, Next Fest in February 2027, and the first two weeks of players
  • Playtest volume, which I cannot run at any scale alone

What I am not asking for

  • Design help. The game works, and I would rather be told it is wrong than have it redesigned
  • An Early Access runway. It ships finished
  • Years. It is close

Where I am flexible

  • Funding, revenue share and recoupment structure, entirely open
  • Platforms beyond Steam, if you see the case. I have not started a port
  • IP stays with Fizzostia. Everything else is a conversation

A playable build is ready now and I will send it the moment you want it, along with Steam keys for as many seats as you want to fill. The trailer and store page predate the money scoring and the new mode names, so the build is the best thing to judge.
